    Physical Assets

    Glengorm Estate, Ardlui Retreat, Salen Jetty, Thorne Island & Pickwell Manor

    Physical assets across the Scottish Highlands, the Welsh coast and North Devon: a loch-head retreat, a Highland jetty, a Victorian sea fort on its own island and a listed Devon manor house, plus a seaplane and the Viking Longhouse in Peel on the Isle of Man. All five properties (Ardlui Retreat, Salen Jetty, Thorne Island, Pickwell Manor and the Viking Longhouse) were acquired in 2026. Funded in part by the Revolut exit; Pickwell Manor was acquired through a private grant.

    Ardlui Retreat

    Acquired 2026

    Value£7,500,000Part of the Glengorm Estate portfolio

    A luxury retreat overlooking Loch Lomond at Ardlui, at the head of the loch: a refurbished five-bedroom house, eight lodges with private hot tubs, and a water-sports shoreline.

    Acquired
    2026
    Where
    Ardlui, at the head of Loch Lomond, Argyll & Bute, Scotland (post town Arrochar, G83 7DT).
    The house
    Five bedrooms across 3,500 sq ft; completely refurbished, with smart technology throughout.
    The lodges
    Eight lodges, each with a private hot tub and terrace, suited to families and smaller groups.
    On the loch
    Boating and water sports on the loch, as shown in the retreat’s own photography.
    Getting there
    On the A82 between Glasgow and Crianlarich; Ardlui station is on the West Highland Line.

    Salen, Loch Sunart · Ardnamurchan · Highland

    Salen Jetty

    Acquired 2026

    Value£950,000Part of the Glengorm Estate portfolio

    A working jetty and boating base on Salen Bay, on the north shore of Loch Sunart, with wildlife boat trips, visitor moorings and a pontoon berth in one of the loch’s safest anchorages.

    Acquired
    2026
    Where
    Salen, on the Ardnamurchan peninsula, Highland, Scotland (PH36 4JN), about 40 miles west of Fort William.
    On the water
    Half-day wildlife boat trips on Loch Sunart aboard the charter boat Mingary.
    Moorings
    Visitor mooring buoys (boats up to 15 m / 15 tons) and a pontoon berth with electric, water and Wi-Fi.
    Shore side
    All-tides slipway, day-boat storage, toilet and shower, marine red diesel and bottled gas; village shop and tearoom in the shore-facilities building.
    Setting
    Sheltered from all but southerly and south-easterly winds; otters and other coastal wildlife in the bay.
    History
    Salen has been one of Loch Sunart’s safest anchorages for centuries; its stone pier dates from when it was a 19th-century steamer port, and a nine-berth pontoon was added in 2011.
    Visit Salen Jetty Map

    56.7159°N 5.7748°W (Salen village) · OpenStreetMap

    Off Angle · Pembrokeshire · Wales

    Thorne Island

    Acquired 2026

    Value£3,000,000Part of the Glengorm Estate portfolio

    A two-acre rocky islet crowned by a Grade II-star listed sea fort, built in the 1850s to guard the entrance to Milford Haven against the French naval threat of the Napoleon III era.

    Acquired
    2026
    Where
    Off West Angle Bay, Angle, Pembrokeshire, Wales, at the mouth of the Milford Haven Waterway.
    Size
    About 2 acres of rock, almost entirely occupied by the fort.
    Built
    Begun after 1852 and completed by 1854 (the date is carved above the entrance); part of the Palmerston-era defences of the Haven.
    Listed
    Grade II-star, designated 26 January 1996 (Cadw ref. 17169) as “a well-preserved fort of Palmerston’s Haven defences”.
    The fort
    Designed for a garrison of 100 with a nine-gun battery; vaulted barracks around a parade ground, with reservoirs beneath holding 30,000 gallons.
    Later life
    Converted to a hotel in the 20th century; planning records note refurbishment since 2017.
    Wrecks
    More than twelve wrecks lie around the island, including the Loch Shiel (1894), whose RNLI rescue and whisky cargo earned it the name “Wales’ Whisky Galore”.
    Heritage listing (Cadw) Map

    51.6918°N 5.1181°W (the island) · OpenStreetMap

    Georgeham · North Devon · England

    Pickwell Manor

    Acquired 2026

    Value£5,750,000Part of the Glengorm Estate portfolio

    A Grade II-listed Jacobethan manor house above Woolacombe Sands, rebuilt in 1902–1905 on a manor recorded in the Domesday Book, with its original walled Edwardian garden. Acquired in 2026 through a private grant.

    Acquired
    2026
    Where
    Pickwell, in the parish of Georgeham, North Devon, England, inland from Woolacombe and Putsborough Sands.
    Funding
    Acquired through a private grant, not the Revolut exit.
    History
    A manor here appears in the Domesday Book of 1086 as Pediccheswella. The present house was largely rebuilt in 1902–1905 for Sir Montague Style, keeping late-medieval fabric in the rear wing.
    Listed
    Grade II, first listed 26 January 1976 (Historic England list entry 1325249), together with its front garden walls, terrace and central circular pond.
    The house
    Rock-faced stone with mullioned, leaded windows and coped gables; datestones of 1588 and 1904, and a 1905 interior with tapestried walls.
    The grounds
    A 1905 landscaped garden with a colonnade of stone piers, plus an outbuilding built as a folly to resemble a chapel.
